objective:
Documentation-only task: bring the project docs in line with the Room schema v1 that is now implemented and committed in core-data (branch feature/room-schema). No code, build, or schema changes.

SOURCE OF TRUTH: the committed code and exported schema, not memory. Read core-data/schemas/com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.data.db.ActivityLedgerDatabase/1.json, the entities/converters/DAOs/ID factory under core-data/src/main/kotlin, the enums under core-domain/src/main/kotlin, and docs/proposals/room-schema/TOOLING_NOTES.md (which records the UUIDv7 evidence). Where the design decisions below and the committed schema disagree, the schema wins and you report the disagreement.

DESIGN DECISIONS TO REFLECT (from the signed-off design spec, section 5):
5.1 Identifiers: UUIDv7 as canonical lowercase 36-char text, via Kotlin stdlib kotlin.uuid.Uuid (experimental opt-in confined to one ID factory), behind an IdFactory interface so tests supply deterministic IDs. Fallback rule: if the V7 generator is unavailable at the pinned Kotlin version, use random UUIDv4 via java.util.UUID; never a third-party UUID library. DB1.1 found Uuid.generateV7() works at Kotlin 2.3.21, so V7 is what shipped.
5.2 activity_occurrences.raw_capture_id has a UNIQUE index (one occurrence per raw capture in schema v1) - cheapest guarantee that a retried acceptance or duplicate watch delivery cannot double-log; a future multi-activity-per-utterance design is a normal migration.
5.3 raw_captures.captured_zone_id TEXT NOT NULL (IANA zone id at capture time); needed so DATE_ONLY / resolved times keep meaning after travel (ADR-018). Occurrences and corrections are resolved in that zone; no further zone columns.
5.4 canonical_activities.normalized_name is a plain non-unique index (merged/archived activities may share a name; Room cannot declare partial unique indexes; preventing duplicate active activities is Step 3 policy). activity_aliases has UNIQUE (canonical_activity_id, normalized_alias).
5.5 Corrections do not fabricate interpretation rows: a user correction writes a corrections row and updates the occurrence; effective_interpretation_id changes only when a real new interpretation is accepted, recorded via the correction's previous/new interpretation columns; corrections.source carries the user-originated flag.
5.6 No SQLite triggers: raw-text immutability is enforced by data-layer API shape plus tests; triggers are not tracked in Room's exported schema so every migration would have to remember to recreate them.
Also: all foreign keys are NO ACTION (no CASCADE / SET NULL) so deleting referenced evidence fails; Room enables foreign_keys itself; enums stored as their Kotlin constant name (text), unknown stored name throws; no fallbackToDestructiveMigration anywhere, guarded by tests; a reusable migration test harness exists (TEST_STRATEGY section 11).

ActivityResolution: EXISTING_ACTIVITY, NEW_ACTIVITY, AMBIGUOUS, UNRESOLVED -> interpretations.activity_resolution
ProcessingState: CAPTURED, QUEUED_FOR_PHONE, TRANSCRIBED, INTERPRETING, INTERPRETED, PERSISTED, NEEDS_REVIEW, FAILED_RETRYABLE, FAILED_FINAL -> raw_captures.processing_state
TimePrecision: EXACT, APPROXIMATE, DATE_ONLY, INFERRED_NOW -> interpretations/occurrences.time_precision, corrections.previous/new_time_precision
VisibilityStatus: ACTIVE, HIDDEN -> occurrences.visibility_status
CanonicalActivityStatus: ACTIVE, MERGED, ARCHIVED -> canonical_activities.status
AliasSource: USER_CORRECTION, AI_CONFIRMED, SEEDED, MANUAL -> activity_aliases.source
CorrectionSource: USER, REINTERPRETATION -> corrections.source
CaptureSource: PHONE_VOICE, PHONE_TEXT, WATCH_VOICE -> raw_captures.source
InterpretationOperation: LOG_ACTIVITY, QUERY_HISTORY, UNSUPPORTED -> interpretations.operation
ValidationStatus: VALID, INVALID, NEEDS_REVIEW -> interpretations.validation_status
ConfidenceBand: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW -> interpretations.model_confidence_band
Verify each against the actual enum source; code wins.
